title: Explorative data collection for non-invasive faecal diagnostics in children
summary:
The aim of this study is to create a meaningful faecal diagnostic profile for children. To this end, reference ranges for intestinal bacteria in children as well as biochemical inflammation and digestive markers that do not yet exist in the literature will be investigated.
The initial aim is to test established diagnostic markers used in adult stool samples in a cohort of healthy children. This will determine whether the same reference values apply as in adults. The intestinal bacteria are analysed by growing bactria on culture media and by detecting the bacterial DNA. Various markers that can indicate inflammation in the intestine are also analysed. In addition, the protein, fat, water and sugar content of the stool samples will be determined. 
The study will include 500 stool samples from children aged 0 to 14 years, taking into account the type of birth and diet.
The second objective is to analyse the above-mentioned markers in children with chronic inflammatory bowel disease, irritable bowel syndrome, allergies or autoimmune diseases. A further 320 stool samples will be collected for this purpose. This data should clarify whether the markers are suitable for diagnosing dysbiosis, intestinal inflammation or reduced digestive performance in children.
This is a purely observational study that is intended to help paediatricians decide in future which stool examinations may be useful for children.
conditions: The clinical conditions specified in the observation groups are included in the study.
